terra.problem: The explanation turns folded hands into the categorical claim that the fool is not working at all.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the verse, with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
The previous verse speaks of labor, success and envy, but does not say money was all over it.
The text says the man's eyes are not content with his wealth; it does not say he is looking for more.
The man's question says he deprives himself of enjoyment, not that he never enjoys his work.
The text does not say the man cannot enjoy any of his work.
The man asks whom he toils for; the text does not say he toils for nobody. It also says two have a good return, not that they get more than one person working alone.
The verse says two have a good return for their labor, not that they necessarily get more from it.
The verse says a companion can lift the fallen person up. It does not say he does so or that he does not help himself to a share.
The verse says a companion can lift the fallen person up, not that the two stick together and he actually does so.
The explanation is generic and ends with a vague claim about the picture sticking in people's heads.
The explanation is flat: it quotes the verse and restates it without a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The text says the king no longer knows how to take a warning; it does not say he is in trouble.
It calls the baker's answer the "wrong mix," contrary to the rule against saying an answer is wrong.
Saying money is not part of the comparison overlooks that the text describes the youth as poor.
The verse says later people will not celebrate this successor. It does not state the universal claim that fame does not last.
The text says later people will not celebrate the successor, not that they will forget him.
